title: Collection Traversal and Mutation Boundary
definition: Collection traversal visits elements according to a defined access order and invariant; mutation during traversal can alter future values, bounds, and visited elements and must be controlled explicitly.
purpose: Design terminating loops that visit exactly the intended elements and preserve collection invariants.
history: Indexed loops, iterators, and higher-order iteration express traversal with different control and mutation trade-offs.
mental_model: A cursor visits positions under a written rule: start, bound, step, current element, and accumulated state.
analogy: Inspecting items on a conveyor; removing or adding items while inspecting can change what reaches the cursor, though language semantics are more precise.
industry_notes: Prefer clear traversal intent and avoid concurrent structural mutation unless semantics are explicitly required and tested.
ai_notes: Ask AI for visited-index trace and mutation behavior, not only final output.
interview_notes: Ask how array modification during traversal changes behavior.
